extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator; general literate public and aspiring essayists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for composing short moral/satirical periodical essays that blend natural imagery, allegory, character-appropriate speech, and measured moral instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use natural imagery to evoke cheerfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sun, which is as the great Soul of the Universe, and produces all the Necessaries of Life, has a particular Influence in chearing the Mind of Man; Those several living Creatures which are made for our Service or Sustenance, at the same time either fill the Woods with their Musick, furnish us with Game, or raise pleasing Ideas in us by the delightfulness of their Appearance, Fountains, Lakes, and Rivers, are as refreshing to the Imagination, as to the Soil through which they pass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy sun, animals, water-features, and pastoral detail to refresh the reader's imagination and induce a cheerful tone. The essay uses these elements as direct means to 'chear' the mind; note also the discussion of colour (green) as visually comforting (painters hang a green cloth to ease the eye) — sensory detail across sight, smell, and sound strengthens the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine usefulness with beauty in description
rubrics_metrics.description: To consider further this double End in the Works of Nature, and how they are at the same time both useful and entertaining, we find that the most important Parts in the vegetable World are those which are the most beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that practical/functional elements can also be sources of beauty; portray objects and actions as both serviceable and aesthetically pleasing (e.g., seeds lodged in flowers). This creates layered meaning and makes description feel purposeful rather than merely ornamental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow delight from apparently useless or grotesque particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Providence has taken care to keep up this Chearfulness in the Mind of Man, by having formed it after such a manner, as to make it capable of conceiving Delight from several Objects which seem to have very little use in them; as from the Wildness of Rocks and Desarts, and the like grotesque Parts of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include wild, grotesque, or superficially 'useless' details (rocks, deserts, oddities) to enrich feeling and wonder; these particulars can generate pleasure and variety even when not strictly 'useful.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep imagery varied through temporal and seasonal change
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reader's own Thoughts will suggest to him the Vicissitude of Day and Night, the Change of Seasons, with all that Variety of Scenes which diversifiy the Face of Nature, and fill the Mind with a perpetual Succession of beautiful and pleasing Images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cycles of time (day/night, seasons) and changing scenes to maintain narrative or descriptive freshness. Succession and variety avoid monotony and sustain the reader's delight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify and read original sources for quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is my Custom, when I read your Papers, to read over the Quotations in the Authors from whence you take them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using quotations or allusions, consult the original texts to ensure accuracy and to capture nuances of tone and meaning. This habit improves fidelity and authority in paraphrase and citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paraphrase/translation should capture the original's tenderness and imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: upon reading it I thought the Ideas so exquisitely soft and tender, that I could not help making this Paraphrase of it; which, now it is done, I can as little forbear sending to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In translating or paraphrasing poetic or biblical passages, aim to preserve the central affect (e.g., tenderness, softness) and the striking images rather than producing a literal but lifeless rendering. Let tone guide choices of diction and imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make speech authentic to character by using appropriate fables and allegories
rubrics_metrics.description: to make him speak in Character, ascribes to him a Speech full of those Fables and Allegories which old Men take Delight in relating, and which are very proper for Instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a character's voice and the kinds of stories or references they use fit their age, station, and temperament. Employing period-appropriate fables/allegories strengthens verisimilitude and instructional force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft allegory so it needs little explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: This noble Allegory needs but little Explanation; for whether the Goddess ATE signifies Injury . . . or divine Justice . . . the Interpretation is obvious enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design allegories and metaphors to be clear and resonant on their own; avoid over-explaining. If an allegory is well-chosen, readers should grasp its moral or point with minimal exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use formal structures to restrain extravagance of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Among other Reasons for set Forms of Prayer, I have often thought it a very good one, that by this means the Folly and Extravagance of Mens Desires may be kept within due Bounds, and not break out in absurd and ridiculous Petitions on so great and solemn an Occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply forms, constraints, or structured devices (set phrases, stanza forms, rhetorical frames) to focus and moderate expression. Formal limits can prevent overwrought or absurd excess and channel creative energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict virtue as inward conscience rather than mere outward shame
rubrics_metrics.description: Modesty consists in being conscious of no Ill, and not in being ashamed of having done it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show characters' inner moral states (conscience, innocence) instead of relying solely on external signs (blushing, ashamed looks). Interiority and consistent action are better indicators of virtue than performative appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not elevate weak or ridiculous opponents by over-arguing them
rubrics_metrics.description: I think reasoning against such Unbelievers upon a Point that shocks the Common Sense of Mankind, is doing them too great an Honour, giving them a Figure in the Eye of the World, and making People fancy that they have more in them than they really have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing manifestly weak or irrational positions, consider mockery, irony, or concise rebuttal rather than prolonged serious debate — excessive engagement may grant undue legitimacy to the opponent's stance.
